paper.title: RewardHarness: Self-Evolving Agentic Post-Training
paper.central_claim: A training-free, self-evolving agentic reward framework that reframes reward modeling as context evolution: from ~100 preference demonstrations it iteratively evolves a library of Skills and Tools (validation-gated) that, injected into a frozen VLM sub-agent, beats larger-data-trained reward models (EditReward) and GPT-5 on EditReward-Bench/GenAI-Bench and yields a better RL reward (FlowGRPO, ImgEdit-Bench 3.52).

signatures.object: Library of Skills (declarative Markdown rubrics) and Tools (procedural Markdown specs routed to a secondary VLM call) used as context for a frozen VLM reward judge; baseline = empty library.
signatures.information: Orchestrator sees sub-agent reasoning chains and ground-truth human preference rankings on ~70 train demos; ~30 demos are used only as validation gate; sub-agent (Qwen2.5-VL-7B / Gemini-2.0-Flash) sees images, instruction and selected library context; test benchmarks invisible.
signatures.operation: Evaluate on train split -> score vs human ranking -> chain analysis of correct and failed chains -> create/modify/deprecate proposal -> apply to candidate snapshot
signatures.conditions: Fixed iteration budget (about 77 iterations); N=100 demos.
signatures.feedback: Human preference labels on demos compared with sub-agent predicted rankings.
signatures.selection_rule: Commit only if validation accuracy strictly exceeds current committed library; otherwise discard and restore snapshot. Later aggressive pruning phase.
signatures.selection_data: Held-out validation split (~30 of the 100 demos) disjoint from the proposal/train split; same split reused each iteration.
signatures.persistence: Committed versioned library, frozen at end (iteration-69 library, 7 entries).
signatures.later_use: Orchestrator retrieves a subset of entries per new input; sub-agent reads them as context on held-out benchmarks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Avg pairwise accuracy 45.7 (Qwen) / 47.4 (Gemini) vs EditReward 42.0 / GPT-5 42.1; +15.4 over raw Qwen.
signatures.failure_boundary: Skill proposals accepted 8.1% vs Tool 41.4%; plateau at 52.5% with 13 entries before pruning; orchestrator dependence and cost unmeasured.

signatures.object: Frozen library-based reward model as RL reward for an image editor (FLUX.2-klein-base-4B via FlowGRPO); this updates editor weights, so it is a downstream utility check of the evaluator, not part of the retained non-weight loop.
signatures.information: Reward scores from RewardHarness vs EditReward; editor evaluated on ImgEdit-Bench.
signatures.conditions: Single run per reward; training prompts/data not described in the text.

gap.author_gap: Reward models for image editing need ~100K+ human preference labels, additional training, give opaque scalar rewards, and cannot be applied to API-only models, whereas humans learn the criteria from a few examples.
gap.checked_gap: The annotation-cost and API-only limits are real and sourced to prior reward-model work, but the 'fixed non-weight object' framing is thin: the changed object is the evaluator's context (library), and 'frozen model can improve via context' is background. The needed counterfactual (same 100 demos used in simpler ways) is absent.
gap.lineage: PickScore/ImageReward/VisionReward/EditReward (SFT reward models) -> context-evolution agents (Reflexion, ExpeL, Voyager, ACE, SkillRL) -> RewardHarness specialises context/skill evolution to multimodal reward judging; tool-augmented LLMs (ReAct, ToolLLM) assume fixed tool sets. Neighbours named from the paper only; no neighbour original text fixed in this batch.
gap.closest_adjacent: Rubric/skill/memory evolution for judges (ACE, ExpeL, SkillRL, Voyager); prompt optimisers (e.g. TextGrad/GEPA-style) are not discussed; few-shot in-context use of the same 100 demos not compared.
gap.residue: Whether library evolution (vs the Claude orchestrator, extra VLM tool calls, or simply few-shot prompting) delivers the gain; cost at inference; reward-hacking robustness.
gap.stakes: Annotation cost for 100K-scale preference data; usability with closed models.
gap.method_response: Failure-attributed library edits gated on a held-out validation split, producing an interpretable library that is frozen and reused.
gap.remaining_gap: Attribution to evolution, orchestrator dependence, cost, other domains (only a +1.1 MMMU hint).
unresolved: Closest adjacent methods not fixed or compared locally.
Which backbone produced the committed library used for the Qwen result (E021).

rs_pattern.reason: Opus: primary adapt_via_conditioning (son55's main card), sub null. The paper's own framing is the card's move: reward capability by conditioning a frozen VLM on a retrieved library instead of training on ~100K labels. C03 is not assigned because there is no upstream phase that teaches the model to parse the format and no category-level holdout (the run's convention since r17b). sol's generative_process_redesign is not kept: the 'fixed component' here is the evaluator's context, and making it editable is the domain-level premise of every harness-RSI paper. The card's tactic (liberating a fixed component of a generative procedure, isolated by a single-mechanism ablation) is not executed.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Opus (sol's level): the committed library is frozen and read on two disjoint benchmarks, against the empty-library configuration, which is the bare sub-agent (Eq. 1: the context is the selected library entries). That meets the run's retained convention (r12b). Scope limits: whether the Table 1 bare-Qwen row used the same prompt protocol is not stated, and the attribution to feedback-driven evolution (vs Claude's prior knowledge or extra tool calls) is scored in E.causality=2.

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The limitation is real and sourced (annotation cost, opacity, API-only models). But the nearest context-evolution neighbours (Reflexion, ExpeL, ACE, SkillRL) are only named, prompt/rubric optimisers for judges are not discussed, and the motivating premise (models can acquire the preference 'from a handful of demonstrations') is never tested against the cheapest reading of it: few-shot use of the same 100 demos. 'Frozen model improves through context' is background, not a gap. The residual bottleneck is only partly bounded: anchor 2.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Error types map to operations (missing criterion → new Skill, wrong rubric application → modify, perceptual hallucination → Tool), proposals go to a candidate snapshot, and the declarative/procedural split is motivated by observed hallucination failures. Not 4: no distinguishing prediction against few-shot prompting or an orchestrator-written rubric, and the root-cause attribution is unvalidated.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The snapshot → validation-gate → restore chain, pruning and the frozen final library are reconstructible. Thin points (both seats): progressive-disclosure retrieval, proposals per iteration, the secondary VLM used by Tools, and which backbone produced the library behind the Qwen row (opus:O01). Shared omission recorded (no rating change): the final commit is dated iteration 69 while the last strict-improvement jump is iterations 58–60 (opus:O02), and the iteration-60 tool-usage-mandate skill is absent from the final library without a recorded removal (opus:O03).

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with sol. EditReward-Bench and GenAI-Bench are established human-preference benchmarks, and the comparison counts are given (133/450/888). But the stated protocol (each K-way ranking converted to pairwise comparisons) cannot produce the reported K=4 values of 3.4–13.5 for every system, because per-comparison chance would be 50%. The metric actually reported is undescribed, and the Avg column mixes it with K=2 and GenAI accuracies (opus:O04). GenAI-Bench size and the ImgEdit-Bench judge are not given. The reward-hacking claim has no measurement (son55:E018).

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with sol. Relevant controls exist: the empty-library configuration (bare Qwen 30.3 / Gemini 38.1 on the test benchmarks, 42.5% on validation), EditReward on the same backbone, and the reward signal swapped inside the same FlowGRPO pipeline. Key gaps keep it at 2, not 1 or 3: no Claude-written library without feedback (the main alternative explanation is the orchestrator's prior knowledge), no gate-off, no skills-vs-tools arm, no same-demos few-shot baseline, unspecified secondary-VLM calls, and a single-run RL margin (3.52 vs 3.45). This follows the r17b Web2BigTable convention: clean store-off plus missing non-feedback arm = 2.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Demonstrations come only from EditReward-Data train, the bench is disjoint, GenAI-Bench is a second benchmark, and MMMU is a held-out split. The 62.5% is selection-set and is not used as a test claim. Not 4: no overlap audit for the foundation models, and the gate reuses a ~30–40-unit split 77 times.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder tier 1): sample sizes and negative information (acceptance rates 8.1%/41.4%, plateau, per-category RL drops) are given. The main results are single-run, with no interval, seed variance or test for margins such as 45.7 vs 44.1 and 3.52 vs 3.45.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with son55. The annotation budget, which is the paper's cost claim (100 demonstrations vs 200K), is quantified and compared with the baselines, and the iteration count (77) is given. Orchestrator/API cost, Tool secondary-VLM calls at inference and a matched-compute baseline are explicitly deferred (§5), so not 2. Not 0: one real cost dimension is reported against the baselines, unlike runs that only list settings.
